subject: POC next steps + workload/profile details — Redwood POC kickoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@saasify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC next steps + workload/profile details — Redwood POC kickoff

Alex — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before the POC kickoff: 

Recap / success criteria (from call)
- Primary goal: evaluate Redwood for realtime user-facing generation on SaaSify search assistants.
- Success criteria: P95 latency <= 500ms for short prompts (target endpoints), model quality parity with current baseline (qualitative eval set), and cost per 1k responses <= $X target (we'll refine).

Workload profile (please confirm or correct)
- Sustained RPS: ~20 RPS across peak hour
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent active users (concurrent inference sessions); expected concurrent model inferences ~40
- Burst patterns: spikes to 200-500 RPS for <2 minutes during marketing events (10-20x baseline bursts expected)
- Prompt lengths: user prompts ~30-150 tokens; expected response lengths ~50-400 tokens (avg ~120)
- Session characteristics: mix of short chat-turns and longer multi-turn flows; KV-cache reuse expected ~50% for repeated prompts

POC plan (proposal)
- Duration: 2 weeks (pilot evaluation window)
- Objectives: throughput/latency validation, integration checklist, quality checks on a seeded eval set, cost projections under expected traffic patterns
- Owners: Ben Carter (commercial), Marissa Cole (solution/technical lead), Alex Johnson (customer POC owner)
- Kickoff: propose Wed 12 May 10:00 PT for an initial runbook review + access exchange

What we need from you before kickoff
1) A short traffic sample (CSV / logs) showing timestamps, endpoint, prompt length, response length, and peak periods — helps us size autoscaling/batching.
2) Priority endpoints (3-5) you want us to validate first.
3) Any redlines/security constraints for test data (PII scope).

I attached a short Redwood POC checklist to speed onboarding.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this going.

— Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Johnson <alex@saasify.com>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC next steps + workload/profile details — Redwood POC kickoff

Ben — thanks for the concise summary. Confirming the numbers below and attaching a 48h traffic sample for the first pass. See inline answers: 

Workload (confirmed)
- Sustained RPS: 18-22 RPS during peak hour (we're send per-endpoint breakdown in CSV).
- Concurrency: ~180-220 concurrent active sessions; model concurrency today is around 35-45 active inferences.
- Burst: typical marketing-related spikes to ~400 RPS lasting 30-90s; rare events hit ~700 RPS for <30s.
- Prompt lengths: median 60 tokens, 95th pct ~200 tokens; responses median 140 tokens, 95th pct ~420 tokens.

Priority endpoints for POC
1) /assistant/search-enhance (highest traffic)
2) /assistant/onboarding-flow (critical latency sensitive)
3) /assistant/custom-qa (lower volume, quality-focused)

Security/data
- Test data may contain hashed user ids but no plain PII in the sample we'll share. Production data is scrubbing-enabled; we can provide a redacted subset for the POC.

Attachments: saasify-traffic-sample.csv (48h export) — columns: timestamp, endpoint, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, user_id_hash

We're good for kickoff Wed 12 May 10:00 PT. Priya (cc'd) will be the day-to-day contact for runbook items and will provide the CSV + a short README for the sample.

— Alex
Head of Product, SaaSify
alex@saasify.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@saasify.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC next steps + workload/profile details — Redwood POC kickoff

Thanks Alex — this is very helpful. A few technical clarifications and proposed POC configuration so we can size capacity and telemetry: 

Clarifying Qs
- Sample granularity: is the CSV sampled at request level (we assume yes). Please include a boolean column for cache_hit if you have it.
- Max tokens per request (hard cap) — can you share current limits? We need worst-case for memory planning.

Proposed POC config (initial)
- Model: redwood-3.0-medium (we'll propose alternatives after first run if latency/quality tradeoffs need it)
- Capacity: equivalent of 4 x A100-class GPUs reserved for the 2-week window (autoscale to +2 gpus for sustained >30 RPS per shard)
- Concurrency tuning: per-worker concurrency target 8-12; global routing to balance latency vs cost
- Warmup: 30 minute warmup period before measured runs; we'll run a replay of your 1-hour peak to validate burst handling
- Instrumentation: please confirm we can get endpoint-level success/failure and latency traces (we'll provide an agent/SDK snippet)

Evaluation plan (what we'll measure)
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 for the three priority endpoints during sustained and burst replays
- Throughput: max sustainable RPS for target P95 threshold
- Quality: run your seeded eval set against the same prompts and collect side-by-side outputs for human review
- Cost: tokens + GPU-hours for the test window so we can forecast unit economics

Ownership & next steps
- Action items for SaaSify: upload CSV + indicate cache_hit column (Priya), confirm max tokens, and share a small seed eval set for quality checks (3-5 representative prompts per endpoint)
- Redwood action items: provision pilot environment, share runbook + SDK snippet, schedule kickoff call Wed 12 May 10:00 PT (invite will follow)

If that all looks good I'll schedule a short 30min runbook review Wed morning and finalize the test plan.

— Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0129
